data.name: Midadi
data.gender_notes: Midadi is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'midad', meaning 'gentleness', 'softness' or 'tenderness'. It is a beautiful name for a girl, evoking images of delicate flowers and gentle breezes. The name Midadi carries the meaning “Gentleness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Midadi usually hope their child will grow to embody gentleness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Midadi is a name that embodies the gentle and compassionate nature of Allah. It is a reminder to be kind, patient and understanding, even in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Midadi belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentleness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Midadi total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_pashto.name: میدادی
in_pashto.meaning: الله تعالیٰ د ځانګړی نوم، چې الله تعالیٰ له لاندې کړې دي
in_pashto.long_meaning: میدادی الله تعالیٰ د ځانګړی نوم دی چې الله تعالیٰ له انسان په لاندې کړې دی. دا نوم له الله تعالیٰ د پخواني نومونو څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې الله تعالیٰ د انسان د لاندې کولو سره څرګند شوی دی. دا نوم په افغانستان کې د بچو لپاره ډیره لېواله دی.

in_english.name: Midadi
in_english.meaning: One of Allah's beautiful names, describing Him as taking care of and guiding Adam's children
in_english.long_meaning: Midadi is one of Allah's beautiful names, describing Him as taking care of and guiding Adam's children. This name is derived from the Arabic root, which means to take care of or guide. In Islamic tradition, this name is given to children as a blessing, and it is also used to describe a man who is committed to his faith and good deeds. The name Midadi is not commonly used in English-speaking countries, but it is popular in many Muslim cultures around the world.
